bib.title: ERNIE: Enhanced Language Representation with Informative Entities
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), pages 1441-1451

question: Can a BERT-style language representation model be improved on knowledge-driven tasks by fusing entity embeddings from a knowledge graph into its layers during pre-training?
hypothesis: Informative entities in KGs can enhance language representation with external knowledge.
contributions: A knowledgeable aggregator (K-Encoder) that fuses token and entity embeddings
A denoising entity auto-encoder (dEA) pre-training task over token-entity alignments
Gains over BERT on entity typing and relation classification, comparable results on GLUE

method.summary: ERNIE stacks a BERT-style T-Encoder (N=6 layers) under a K-Encoder (M=6 aggregators) that fuses token embeddings with TransE entity embeddings aligned by TAGME/Wikidata links. It is pre-trained on English Wikipedia aligned to Wikidata with MLM, NSP and a new dEA entity-prediction loss, then fine-tuned with marker tokens for entity typing and relation classification.
method.task: Knowledge-enhanced language representation pre-training; entity typing, relation classification, GLUE

datasets.name: English Wikipedia aligned to Wikidata
datasets.preprocessing: sentences with fewer than 3 entities discarded

datasets.name: Wikidata subset for TransE
datasets.preprocessing: TransE embeddings (dim 100) used as fixed entity inputs

datasets.name: FIGER
datasets.source: Ling et al. 2015; train distantly supervised, test human annotated

datasets.name: FewRel
datasets.split: rearranged from few-shot setting: 100 instances per class for train, 200 per class for dev and test
datasets.preprocessing: facts related to FewRel dropped from the KG before pre-training

datasets.name: GLUE (8 datasets)
datasets.size: MNLI 392k, QQP 363k, QNLI 104k, SST-2 67k, CoLA 8.5k, STS-B 5.7k, MRPC 3.5k, RTE 2.5k

models.name: ERNIE
models.architecture: T-Encoder (BERT Transformer) + K-Encoder of aggregators with token and entity multi-head attention and an information fusion layer
models.init_from: Google BERT released parameters for the Transformer blocks that encode tokens; entity encoding modules randomly initialised

other.entity_alignment: entity aligned to first token of its named-entity phrase

training.objective: sum of dEA, MLM and NSP losses; dEA is cross-entropy over entities in the given sequence (Eq. 7); 5% of alignments get a random entity, 15% are masked, rest unchanged
training.optimizer: Adam (fine-tuning stated; pre-training largely follows BERT)
training.epochs: pre-training 1 epoch; fine-tuning 3 to 10; FIGER 2 or 3

other.note: other pre-training hyper-parameters 'largely follow' BERT without values given

inference.samples: not stated (single results reported, no seeds or variance)
inference.prompting: Fine-tuning input: [CLS] for common tasks; [ENT] marks around mention for entity typing; [HD] and [TL] marks around head and tail for relation classification; [CLS] output used for classification
inference.retrieval: Entity mentions linked to KG entities with TAGME (Ferragina and Scaiella 2010) because most datasets lack entity annotations

metrics.name: Strict accuracy / loose macro / loose micro (FIGER)
metrics.definition: strict accuracy is the ratio of instances whose predictions are identical to human annotations

metrics.name: Macro P/R/F1 (FewRel)
metrics.definition: macro averaged because FewRel has no null instances

baselines: BERT fine-tuned with same input format
eval.protocol: Single reported numbers; no significance test or seeds stated. CNN, PA-LSTM and C-GCN TACRED numbers taken from Zhang et al. 2018.

results.claim: ERNIE improves FewRel relation classification macro F1 over BERT by about 3.4 points.
results.setup: FewRel rearranged to 100 train / 200 dev / 200 test instances per class, 80 classes, fine-tuned from BERT-initialised ERNIE, macro averaged; FewRel-related facts removed from the KG before pre-training
results.quote: ERNIE achieves an absolute F1 increase of 3.4% over BERT
results.table: Table 5, row ERNIE, column FewRel F1

results.claim: ERNIE improves TACRED micro F1 over BERT by nearly 2 points and has the best recall and F1.
results.setup: TACRED 68,124 train, 42 relations, micro averaged, entities linked with TAGME
results.quote: increases the F1 of BERT by nearly 2.0%
results.table: Table 5, row ERNIE, column TACRED F1

results.claim: On FIGER (distantly supervised) ERNIE raises strict accuracy over BERT by about 5 points; authors read this as KG knowledge regularising against noisy labels.
results.setup: FIGER, 2M distantly labelled train, 563 human-annotated test, batch 2048, 2 or 3 epochs
results.quote: indicating the external knowledge regularizes ERNIE to avoid ﬁtting the noisy labels

results.claim: On Open Entity ERNIE reaches F1 75.56 versus 73.56 for BERT.
results.setup: Open Entity, 2,000 train / dev / test, 6 types, fine-tuned with [ENT] marks

results.claim: Ablation: removing entity input at fine-tuning keeps FewRel F1 at 85.79 and removing dEA gives 85.62; both lose most of the gain over BERT (84.89), so the full model needs both.
results.setup: FewRel, same rearranged split; w/o entities = fine-tuning without entity sequence input, w/o dEA = pre-training without dEA
results.quote: which increases the F1 score of BERT by 0.9%
results.table: Table 7, row w/o entities, column F1

results.claim: ERNIE is comparable to BERT-BASE on GLUE: same on QQP and SST-2, slightly lower on MNLI, better on CoLA and RTE, worse on STS-B and MRPC.
results.setup: 8 GLUE datasets, leaderboard submissions, BERT numbers from the leaderboard
results.quote: In short, ERNIE achieves comparable results with BERTBASE on GLUE.

results.claim: Knowledge module adds about 4M parameters over BERT-BASE (114M vs 110M).

results.setup: Wikidata sample with 5,040,986 entities used for TransE; corpus nearly 4,500M subwords and 140M entities
results.quote: we sample part of Wikidata which contains 5, 040, 986 entities and 24, 267, 796 fact triples

limits: Only English Wikipedia and a Wikidata subset; authors list ConceptNet and other knowledge sources, feature-based models and larger annotated corpora as future work.
Initialised from BERT-BASE rather than trained from scratch because of cost; pre-trained one epoch only; max sequence length cut to 256.
Entities are fixed TransE vectors (dim 100) over only the entity-linked tokens; alignment errors from TAGME are handled only heuristically via dEA noise (5% random, 15% masked).
No seeds, variance or significance tests; BERT baseline is the authors' fine-tuning of BERT with the same marker input.
Ablation done only on FewRel; the ablation shows the gain depends on both dEA and entity input, and the 'w/o dEA' variant gains only 0.7 F1 over BERT.
GLUE shows no benefit and some losses; authors say GLUE does not require external knowledge.
Reproducibility: warmup, schedule, weight decay, dropout, hardware and compute not stated.
Text KG is used as embeddings, not as graph structure or retrieval at inference; not a KG-RAG method.

terms.definition: randomly masks some token-entity alignments and requires the system to predict all corresponding entities based on aligned tokens
underlying textual encoder for lexical and syntactic information, and upper knowledgeable encoder that integrates token-oriented knowledge into textual information
